Therefore, one should not grasp at phenomena, nor should one grasp at non-phenomena. Because of this meaning, the Tathagata <note>original: "如來", an epithet for the Buddha meaning "Thus-Come One"</note> always says: "You monks! Know that my teaching is like a raft. Even the dharma <note>original: "法", here referring to Buddhist teachings</note> should be abandoned; how much more so that which is not the dharma."

### The Seventh Section: On Neither Attainment Nor Discourse

Subhuti! What do you think? Has the Tathagata attained the <term>anuttara-samyak-sambodhi</term> <gloss>unsurpassed, complete, perfect enlightenment</gloss>? Does the Tathagata have any fixed teaching?

Subhuti replied: As I understand the meaning of what the Buddha has said, there is no fixed teaching called <term>anuttara-samyak-sambodhi</term>, nor is there any fixed teaching that the Tathagata can state. Why is this? The teachings stated by the Tathagata are all intangible, inexpressible, neither phenomena nor non-phenomena. Why is this? All sages and worthies are distinguished by the <term>asamskrta-dharma</term> <gloss>unconditioned or uncompounded reality</gloss>.

### The Eighth Section: Birth Through the Dharma

Subhuti! What do you think? If someone were to fill the three-thousand-great-thousand world systems with the seven treasures <note>traditional Buddhist symbols of wealth including gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, agate, ruby, and cornelian</note> and give them as alms, would that person obtain many merits?

Subhuti replied: Very many, World-Honored One! Why? Because this merit is not the essence of merit itself; therefore, the Tathagata speaks of the merit as being great.

If, however, there were another person who accepted and held even a four-line verse of this sutra and explained it to others, their merit would be greater than the former. Why? Subhuti! All the Buddhas and the <term>anuttara-samyak-sambodhi</term> of all Buddhas originate from this sutra. Subhuti! What is called the Buddhadharma is itself not the Buddhadharma.

### The Ninth Section: On One Mark and No Mark

<summary>This text emphasizes the emptiness of phenomena and teachings, explaining that true enlightenment is beyond fixed forms and that propagating the sutra holds greater merit than material offerings.</summary>
